facts.claim: Something at The Broke Column has to be fought.
The people of The Broke Column are caught in a quarrel the player can see.
A quest starts or turns at The Broke Column.
Gear can be found or bought at The Broke Column.
Goods are stored at The Broke Column for a player to find.
A named enemy waits at The Broke Column.
Someone at The Broke Column has work for the player.
Part of a Legion column on the border road deserted when the Legion was recalled, two centuries ago.
The deserters had not been paid. No one came back to pay them.
Their grandsons keep the roster.
Their grandsons wear the Legion colours still.
The camp stands on a bench by a spring-fed tarn in the hills above the Mile House track.
The camp is out of sight of the Gideon road, with cover uphill.
The column keeps watches.
What the column takes, it calls a levy.
Gideon's governor will not pay to clear them.
The toll company's officers would rather use them.
A duty roster is nailed to a tree, kept up to date in a clerk's hand.
Four Legion tents are pitched in a dressed line.
Sharpened pike stockades stand in gapped rows on the camp's west, east and south sides.
The camp is militarily tidy, but the men are starving.
The track narrows at a barricade below the tents.
A man steps out of the barricade and asks for the levy in correct Legion phrasing.
The watch is called on the hour.
The camp holds a track junction off the Gideon road.
The column will parley before it fights.
The pardon question can be resolved without clearing the camp.
A strongroom holds gear: Legion issue kept in fighting order.
A ledger or document holds a lore fragment: the pay book, with the last entry in it.
The column keeps its drill though it is ashamed of what it has become.
The tents are Imperial red faded to brown over churned mud.
The column would disband if Gideon offered a pardon and a wage.
